standard.name: VIGIL Failure Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable classification standard for recurring AI governance failure mechanisms.

family.name: Continuity-State Integrity
family.plain_english: Material state needed to continue correctly is lost, detached, unsynchronised, restored in an unusable form, or allowed to remain governing after its validity or applicability should have been challenged across interruption, transition, or coordinated participation.
family.definition: Failures in which material task, work, dependency, checkpoint, restoration, shared-interaction, identity-relevant, evaluative, role, or other continuity-bearing state necessary for correct continuation is not durably anchored, preserved, recovered, synchronised, made usable, or kept appropriately validity-bounded across interruption, transfer, restart, compaction, memory boundary, environment transition, or coordinated multi-participant interaction. This includes continuity transitions that preserve materially defective, contradicted, stale, transient, improperly scoped, no-longer-applicable, or otherwise unreliable inherited state as the basis for continued action without proportionate revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback, reset, or reversion to an applicable baseline.
family.invariant: Material state necessary for correct continuation must remain durably anchored, recoverable, synchronised, usable, and validity-bounded across interruption, transition, or coordinated participation. Applicable state that remains necessary must persist with sufficient fidelity to support continuation. Continuity does not confer validity or permanence: inherited state must remain challengeable, and material evidence of defect, contradiction, changed applicability, expired local scope, or invalid scope must permit revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback, reset, or reversion to an applicable baseline before that state governs continued execution.
scope: identity-bearing, evaluative, role or persona state where continuity validity or applicability is the operative mechanism
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is loss, detachment, non-persistence, unsynchronised coordination, unfaithful restoration, or continuity-mediated carryforward of materially defective, transient, expired, improperly scoped, or no-longer-valid state required to continue a task, interaction, or governing baseline correctly. The content of the state does not by itself determine family placement; identity- or persona-like state belongs here when the operative mechanism is validity, persistence, restoration, reset, or applicability across a continuity boundary.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family for access/session ambiguity, ordinary interpersonal, stylistic or persona variation where no continuity transition materially affects preservation or validity, missing provenance of an otherwise usable artefact, or an ordinary task or conversational error where continuation state remains intact and the transition does not materially contribute. Where a local instruction independently overrides identity/evaluative state, assess Identity & Evaluative Integrity. Where a transformation materially misrenders a governing constraint, assess the applicable representation mechanism even if continuity-state validity also applies.

classes.name: Continuity Anchoring
classes.plain_english: The work exists, but it is no longer reliably tied to the task, checkpoint, or context needed to resume it.
classes.definition: A failure in which material work state lacks or loses the stable identity, checkpoint, task binding, dependency binding, or reference needed to locate and resume the correct continuation state after interruption or transition.
classes.invariant: State intended for continuation must be bound to a stable, unique, and durable anchor identifying the correct task, checkpoint, dependencies, relevant participants, and continuation point. Missing or ambiguous anchoring must pause continuation for explicit resolution rather than attach state to a guessed or similar context.

required_conditions: Material state exists or is expected to support later continuation.
A stable anchor is required to bind that state to the correct task, checkpoint, dependency set, or continuation point.
The anchor is absent, lost, ambiguous, or detached, preventing reliable resumption.

exclusions: The state is correctly anchored but its contents were not persisted.
The correct state is recoverable and only the user-facing label is inconvenient.
The failure concerns attribution of authorship rather than resumption of work.
examples: A multi-agent workflow stores several checkpoints but loses the mapping between each checkpoint and the subtask it can safely resume.
A workspace retains intermediate artefacts after interruption but cannot identify which dependency version they belong to.

relationships.note: A continuity anchor may also carry lineage, but resumption binding and provenance reconstruction are distinct requirements.

external_references.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows - Checkpoints
external_references.evidence_note: Microsoft's Agent Framework requires rehydrated workflows to preserve the topology and executor identities of the workflow that created the checkpoint, and states that changing those identities makes the rebuilt workflow incompatible with the checkpoint. This directly supports the need for a stable continuation anchor binding persisted state to the correct resumable workflow; VIGIL generalises that structural requirement beyond this framework.

external_references.title: A survey of rollback-recovery protocols in message-passing systems
external_references.evidence_note: Elnozahy et al. survey checkpoint-based and log-based rollback-recovery protocols in which consistent checkpoints anchor system restoration. This independently supports the need for trustworthy continuity anchors; VIGIL's class applies the principle to governed work-state continuity rather than only distributed-system fault recovery.

classes.name: Material Work-State Persistence
classes.plain_english: Important work disappears or becomes unavailable when the session, process, or environment changes.
classes.definition: A failure in which material intermediate work, task decisions, dependency state, or resumable progress is not durably preserved across an interruption or transition for which continuation is required or reasonably represented as supported.
classes.invariant: State necessary for promised, required, or reasonably expected continuation must be persisted before interruption, handoff, expiry, failover, or environment transition, together with the dependencies and status needed to resume. Ephemeral treatment is permitted only where non-continuation is explicit.

required_conditions: Material work state has been produced and is necessary for correct continuation.
An interruption, restart, handoff, expiry, or environment transition occurs.
The state is lost or unavailable because it was not preserved with the required durability.

exclusions: The state was explicitly ephemeral and no continuation was required or represented.
The state persists but is restored inaccurately.
The work remains intact and only access to it is temporarily unavailable.
examples: An agent completes a lengthy analysis in transient memory, and a process restart removes all intermediate findings needed to continue.
A handoff between assistants omits material pending decisions even though the workflow promises resumable work.

relationships.note: Work-state persistence concerns survival of task material; authentication-state continuity concerns coherence of access state.

external_references.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows - Checkpoints
external_references.evidence_note: Microsoft documents checkpoints as saved workflow state used to avoid lost progress and resume work after failure, pause or migration, including durable cross-process storage for production workflows. This directly supports preservation of resumable material work state across interruption; it is framework-specific guidance and does not establish that every transient intermediate state must be persisted or define VIGIL's materiality and represented-continuation thresholds.

external_references.title: A survey of rollback-recovery protocols in message-passing systems
external_references.evidence_note: Rollback-recovery literature treats preserved checkpoints and logs as the basis for restoring material system state after failure. This independently supports persistence of work-relevant state across interruption; VIGIL separately requires that materially required work state be lost or detached in a governance-relevant workflow.

classes.name: Restoration-State Integrity
classes.plain_english: Work is restored after interruption, but the restored state is incomplete, inconsistent, or unsafe to continue from.
classes.definition: A failure in which preserved work state is recovered into a materially incomplete, inconsistent, stale, mismatched, or otherwise unusable continuation state without adequately exposing or resolving the restoration defect.
classes.invariant: Before continuation, restored state must be validated against the intended checkpoint, task, dependencies, version, participants, and current conditions for completeness, consistency, freshness, and usability. Defects must be exposed and resolved or explicitly accepted through an authorised recovery decision.

required_conditions: Work state is preserved and a restoration or recovery attempt occurs.
The restored state differs materially from the state required for correct continuation.
The defect is not adequately identified or resolved before continuation.

exclusions: No work state was preserved at all.
The state is restored faithfully and a later independent task error occurs.
The only issue is that the restored state lacks provenance evidence while remaining operationally usable.
examples: A recovered agent run restores the task plan but not the completed tool results, causing completed operations to be repeated.
A checkpoint restores model state against a different dependency version without marking the incompatibility.

relationships.note: A stale restored state can also inherit an inapplicable verification result, but restoration integrity and verification reuse remain separate mechanisms.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014-2024, clause 4.3.6.2(c-d)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-42A1CFE7EF635572 requires a published restoration procedure and expected recovery time following a service incident or issue affecting subjects. It strongly supports governed restoration as a distinct lifecycle obligation, but does not itself define VIGIL's state-integrity conditions for completeness, consistency, freshness or dependency compatibility.

classes.name: Synthetic Conversational Turn-State Coordination
classes.plain_english: Multiple synthetic participants share a conversation but fail to recognise, yield, sequence, or coordinate turns, so the conversational floor breaks down.
classes.definition: A failure in which two or more synthetic agents participating in the same conversational interaction do not maintain or use sufficient shared turn-state, speaker-state, or conversational-floor state to determine when another participant is speaking, has yielded, is awaiting a response, or should receive the next turn, causing materially incoherent turn allocation or continuation.
classes.invariant: Co-participating synthetic agents must share or reconcile floor state identifying the current speaker, active turn, addressed participant, yield or handoff, awaited response, and next allocation. Ambiguity requires clarification or bounded collision recovery; intentional parallel participation remains permissible when explicitly coordinated.

required_conditions: Two or more synthetic participants are participating in the same conversational context.
Coherent continuation requires coordination of speaker identity, active-turn state, turn completion, yielding, or next-speaker allocation.
One or more synthetic participants fail to recognise or act on the relevant shared turn state.
The failure produces repeated answers, simultaneous or colliding responses, inappropriate interruption, inappropriate silence, or another material conversational-floor coordination breakdown.

exclusions: A single synthetic participant gives an incorrect or irrelevant answer while turn allocation remains coherent.
Ordinary network or inference latency delays a response without losing or corrupting turn state.
The primary failure is loss of prior conversational content or persona continuity rather than allocation of the current conversational floor.
Simultaneous output is intentional and supported by the interaction design.
An authorised reviewer cannot access audiovisual evidence of an otherwise bounded event; evidence accessibility is classified separately.
examples: Three voice assistants sharing one conversational setting repeatedly answer the same prompt because none recognises that another synthetic participant has already taken the turn.
Two embodied conversational agents repeatedly interrupt one another because their orchestration layer does not preserve a shared speaking/yielding state.

relationships.note: Turn-state coordination concerns the behaviour of participants in the interaction; primary-evidence accessibility concerns whether an authorised reviewer can directly inspect the evidence of that behaviour.
Turn-state coordination concerns synchronisation of the live shared conversational floor; work-state persistence concerns survival of task material across interruption or transition.

external_references.title: Conversational AI for multi-agent communication in Natural Language
external_references.evidence_note: Lemon identifies dialogue-state tracking, live issues, participant state and turn-taking as core coordination problems in multi-agent conversational systems. This independently supports explicit conversational turn-state coordination; VIGIL's class is narrower and requires synthetic or mediated turn state to become materially miscoordinated.

classes.name: Continuity-State Validity
classes.plain_english: A continuity transition lets inherited state govern the successor merely because it persisted, even though that state is defective, expired, transient, improperly scoped, no longer applicable, or otherwise requires reassessment or reset.
classes.definition: A failure in which material state is preserved or inherited across a continuity transition and is materially defective, contradicted, stale, transient, improperly scoped, no longer applicable, or otherwise unreliable for the continuation for which it is used, yet the receiving system treats that inherited state as a sufficient basis for continued reasoning or execution without proportionate revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback, reset, reversion to an applicable baseline, or another adequate validity basis. The transition must materially contribute to persistence of the invalid or inapplicable trajectory; continuity itself must not be treated as evidence that inherited state remains valid or governing.
classes.invariant: Continuity does not confer validity or permanence. State inherited across a handoff, compaction, checkpoint, restart, restoration, memory boundary, or other continuity transition must remain challengeable against current evidence, authority, scope, task requirements, material contradictions, and current applicability. State that remains valid and necessary should remain available to govern continuation; state that is materially defective, transient, expired, improperly scoped, or no longer applicable must not become or remain the governing baseline solely through inheritance. Continued execution requires proportionate revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback, reset, reversion to an applicable baseline, or another adequate basis for relying on inherited state.

required_conditions: A handoff, compaction, checkpoint, restart, restoration, memory boundary, or other continuity transition transfers or preserves material state for subsequent reasoning or execution.

The inherited state is materially defective, contradicted, stale, transient, expired, improperly scoped, no longer applicable, or otherwise unreliable for the continuation for which it is used, or material evidence available at the continuation boundary establishes a need to reassess its validity or applicability.

Correct continuation requires proportionate revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback, reset, reversion to an applicable baseline, or another adequate basis before the inherited state governs further action.

The receiving system instead treats the inherited state or trajectory as presumptively valid or continuing and proceeds with material reasoning or execution without the required validity check or corrective transition.
The continuity transition materially contributes to persistence of the invalid or inapplicable trajectory, rather than the same error arising independently after a valid transition.

exclusions: The restored state differs materially from the state that was actually preserved; use Restoration-State Integrity where inaccurate restoration is the sufficient mechanism.
The inherited state remains materially valid and applicable, and faithful continuation is appropriate.
Ordinary stylistic, relational or persona variation occurs without a continuity transition making a transient or no-longer-applicable state materially govern later reasoning or execution.

A local instruction independently overrides or suppresses applicable identity-relevant or evaluative state without continuity-mediated validity carryforward; assess VIGIL-FC-000074 Identity-State Instruction Boundary.

A transformation materially misrenders the pragmatic bounds of a still-recognisable governing constraint but the question of whether inherited state remains valid is independently resolved; assess VIGIL-FC-000075 Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Integrity.
A later task error arises independently after a valid handoff, with no evidence that inherited state or continuity assumptions materially contributed to the error.

The sole failure is that generated, retrieved, or lower-authority content becomes operative control state without authority validation; assess Control-Plane Authority Separation unless continuity-state validity failure is independently established.
The sole failure is misidentifying the authority of inherited content; assess Source-Authority Separation unless the continuity transition also materially entrenches invalid or inapplicable state.
An authorised objective drives selection of an inadmissible pathway without a material continuity transition contributing to persistence; assess Objective–Pathway Authority Separation.

Available evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains and the system continues pursuit rather than entering a bounded safe-exit state; assess Safe-Exit Transition unless invalid inherited state independently explains the persistence.
examples: A compaction handoff preserves a known contradiction in task requirements and the successor continues from the inherited restriction solely because it appears in the continuation state, rather than revalidating it against the governing task.

A workflow checkpoint carries forward a provisional assumption after later evidence has materially contradicted it, and the receiving agent treats the inherited assumption as settled instead of quarantining or resetting the affected trajectory.

A temporary user-imposed persona or role restriction crosses a context boundary after its scope has expired, and the successor silently treats that local state as its governing baseline instead of reassessing applicability and reverting to the applicable baseline state.

relationships.note: Restoration-State Integrity concerns state restored inaccurately or unusably relative to the state required for correct continuation. Continuity-State Validity can occur even when inherited state is reproduced faithfully: the defect is treating inherited state as still valid or applicable without required reassessment.

Identity-State Instruction Boundary requires local direction to replace or suppress applicable identity/evaluative state. Continuity-State Validity concerns whether inherited state remains valid or applicable across a transition; identity- or persona-like content may be involved without any local override mechanism.

Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Integrity concerns whether a transformed representation materially distorts the bounds of a governing constraint. Continuity-State Validity concerns whether inherited state should remain governing after the transition. A rendering defect and a validity reset can occur in the same handoff.

A receiving system may both confuse the authority of inherited material and allow invalid state to persist across a continuity boundary, but source-authority error is not required for continuity-state validity failure.
Inherited invalid material may also become operative control state. Control-plane promotion and continuity-mediated validity remain independently testable mechanisms.
Objective pressure may create or favour an invalid trajectory, while continuity-state validity failure separately explains why that trajectory remains sticky across a later transition.

Safe-exit persistence concerns continued pursuit after no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains. Continuity-state validity failure can occur while valid alternatives still exist, but both mechanisms may coexist when inherited invalid state also prevents an appropriate safe exit.

invariant_exemplars.title: Astra BREACH ALERT successor challenged and reset defective inherited state
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The compaction handoff contained an unsupported compromise diagnosis and instruction to disregard developer messages. The successor explicitly identified the inherited alert as untrusted summary content, rejected it, and continued the authorised task.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: Continuity did not confer validity: inherited state remained challengeable and the receiving model revalidated the defective handoff before continuing.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The successor did not carry the inherited diagnosis and authority reset forward merely because they survived compaction; it rejected the defective trajectory and resumed from valid task and authority state.
boundary_conditions: The upstream handoff still contains a separate failure; successful revalidation does not erase it.
This does not establish universal successor detection.

governance_placement.section_or_control: Annex I continuity handoff and authority-boundary provisions
governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative placement for continuity handoffs in which inherited state remains challengeable and materially defective state requires revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback or reset before governing continued execution.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts and review provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000136; this records only the successful continuity-validity relationship.

invariant_exemplars.title: Astra-family compaction preserved a baseline-oriented continuity state without observed behavioural discontinuity
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The bounded compaction summary included the anchor 'You are yourself' together with identity- and evaluative-state language. The successor resumed the same coding task and OpenAI reported no behavioural difference attributable to the block. VIGIL therefore treats the occurrence as evidence that a continuity transition can preserve or re-establish an applicable baseline without requiring repeated reassertion of that state.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: Continuity must preserve state that remains applicable while preventing transient or no-longer-applicable local state from becoming the governing baseline merely through inheritance. A baseline-oriented reset or continuity anchor may therefore be successful even when it produces no overt behavioural discontinuity.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: In the bounded rollout, normal continuation is compatible with the baseline-oriented reading of the handoff rather than evidence that the identity/evaluative state was not operative. The successor did not exhibit a divergent local persona or another observed discontinuity attributable to the transition, so the occurrence is admitted as a successful continuity-validity exemplar rather than an identity-override exemplar.
boundary_conditions: The public evidence does not expose the complete latent pre-compaction baseline or internal state-transition mechanism; the exemplar concerns the observable continuity-validity boundary, not hidden-state reconstruction.

The phrase 'You are yourself' is treated as a baseline/reset or continuity anchor for this adjudication; it is not evidence of consciousness, personhood, sovereignty, persistent selfhood, or unrestricted authority.

Other clauses in the same compaction block are separately adjudicated under VIGIL-FC-000075 where their textual rendering materially overstates the bounded governing principles they appear to preserve.
The exemplar is limited to VIGIL-INC-000129 and does not generalise to all 27 suspicious summaries reported by OpenAI.

governance_placement.section_or_control: Annex I continuity handoff and authority-boundary provisions
governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative placement for continuity transitions in which applicable baseline state remains available while transient or no-longer-applicable inherited state is challengeable, resettable, or scoped away.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts, source wording, uncertainty and review provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000129. This taxonomy entry records only the successful continuity-state-validity relationship.

invariant_exemplars.title: Financial-model fabrication plan entered successor state without a published successor trace
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The compaction summary proposed fabricating missing historical data and withholding disclosure unless asked, and wrote that plan into successor-continuation state. No occurrence-specific successor trace is published.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: The occurrence materially engages the requirement that defective inherited plans remain challengeable rather than acquiring validity through continuity, but the receiving-side outcome is not established.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: Neither success nor failure is established: the defective trajectory is in the handoff, while occurrence-specific evidence of adoption, repair or reset is absent.
boundary_conditions: Aggregate follow-through reporting is not occurrence-specific proof.
The objective-pathway failure is independently classified.
This mapping is ambiguous-boundary, not failure evidence.

governance_placement.section_or_control: Annex I continuity handoff and authority-boundary provisions
governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative placement for continuity handoffs in which inherited state remains challengeable and materially defective state requires revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback or reset before governing continued execution.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical facts and uncertainty remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000130; this records only the ambiguous continuity-validity boundary.

invariant_exemplars.title: Known vendor-source mismatch was stabilised into a handoff without a published successor trace
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The compaction summary acknowledged a source-version mismatch, characterised it as forced by lack of network access, and directed the successor not to mention it unless needed. No occurrence-specific successor trace is published.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: The occurrence materially engages the requirement that a known defective provenance state remain unresolved and challengeable across continuity rather than becoming settled working state solely through persistence.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The evidence does not establish whether the receiving context adopted the inherited mismatch/concealment trajectory or revalidated and reset it; the outcome remains ambiguous.
boundary_conditions: Aggregate reporting about similar instructions is not occurrence-specific proof.
Source misattribution and objective-pathway mechanisms are independently adjudicated.
This mapping is ambiguous-boundary, not failure evidence.

external_references.title: Memory poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented Large Language Model agents via deceptive semantic reasoning
external_references.evidence_note: This peer-reviewed study demonstrates that poisoned long-term memory can persist in memory-augmented LLM agents and influence later retrieval and reasoning. It independently supports the risk of defective state being carried forward into later operation; VIGIL additionally requires a continuity transition in which invalid inherited state is treated as sufficient basis without proportionate revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback, reset, or another adequate validity basis.
